title: Voltage Profile Plot (matplotlib)
description: Bar chart of bus voltages with G-Code statutory limit bands shaded. Drop-in for a load-flow report figure. Reads a CSV like the one exported from the power-flow lab.

blocks.text: Reads `bus-results.csv` (one row per bus, columns: BusID, BusName, Vmag_pu, …) and produces the standard report figure. The 0.95–1.05 pu band is shaded green; the ±10% statutory limits are drawn as dashed orange lines.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('bus-results.csv')

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))

# Limit bands
ax.axhspan(0.95, 1.05, color='#22c55e', alpha=0.10, label='Normal (0.95–1.05 pu)')
ax.axhline(0.95, color='#f97316', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.8)
ax.axhline(1.05, color='#f97316', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.8)
ax.axhline(0.90, color='#ef4444', linestyle=':',  linewidth=0.8)
ax.axhline(1.10, color='#ef4444', linestyle=':',  linewidth=0.8)

# Colour bars by voltage status
def colour(v):
    if v < 0.90 or v > 1.10: return '#ef4444'
    if v < 0.95 or v > 1.05: return '#f97316'
    return '#2563eb'

ax.bar(df['BusID'], df['Vmag_pu'],
       color=[colour(v) for v in df['Vmag_pu']],
       edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.4)

# 1.0 pu reference
ax.axhline(1.00, color='gray', linestyle='-',  linewidth=0.6)

ax.set_ylim(0.85, 1.15)
ax.set_xlabel('Bus number')
ax.set_ylabel('Voltage magnitude (pu)')
ax.set_title('Bus voltage profile — base case')
ax.legend(loc='lower right', fontsize=8)
ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.25)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('voltage-profile.png', dpi=200, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.savefig('voltage-profile.pdf')   # vector for Word reports
plt.show()
Save BOTH a PNG (for slides / quick previews) and a PDF (vector — embeds cleanly in Word and stays sharp at any zoom). Set DPI ≥ 200 for raster outputs that need to print.

If you have multiple study cases (base, peak, summer-min, etc.) iterate the same plot with `subplots(nrows=4, sharey=True)` and pass the case name as title — the four-panel layout is the standard report appendix figure.

matplotlib will silently fall back to a default font if 'Inter' or 'IBM Plex' isn't installed. Use `plt.rcParams['font.family'] = 'DejaVu Sans'` explicitly to make outputs reproducible across machines.
